future_check: After any header-layout change, compare all canonical pairs and require every ordinary row-1 cell to belong to one of exactly K equal-width nonzero runs.
rationale: The Racket rule only needs the row-1 color sequence, so sparse markers can execute, but they do not visually teach the same block grammar as the canonical examples. Full runs make source and destination block boundaries explicit and prevent zero padding from becoming a shortcut.
summary: Destination headers use full equal-width runs, matching every canonical input rather than sparse one-cell markers.

future_check: Have the independent monitor decide whether this task should allocate more probability to the canonical 6x6, 6x8, and 6x12/related profiles without reducing axis coverage.
rationale: The repaired distribution deliberately spans K=2..6, body rows=3..9, and block widths=2..5, so only a minority of draws match the three small canonical shapes exactly. The stronger task-linked predicate passes 600/600 and every canonical input is accepted, but intake should retain the warning rather than interpreting the process exit alone as a clean profile signal.
summary: The strict profile gate passes but reports low exact-profile and envelope support under its generic scale heuristic.

future_check: If the oracle changes to consume destination positions or widths, re-open this decision and add canonical examples that disambiguate the new semantics.
rationale: The authoritative program maps each destination color back to the row-0 source run and copies that source run's columns. It never uses the destination run width as a second geometry. Unequal row-1 widths may execute, but they weaken the intended visual grammar, so self_check rejects them and the generator keeps them equal to source widths.
summary: Destination run widths are pedagogical block delimiters, not independent output-width instructions.
